subject: english
question:
The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer.

Can you not / knock so louder / in the morning?
solution:
The erroneous part is: **knock so louder**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• **Knock **is a **verb** in the given sentence i.e. **"Can you not knock so louder in the morning??"**
 
• We know that,
 
 
• The **-er **form with a word is used after **nouns or noun phrases.**
 
• The **-ly** form with a verb is used after **verbs.**
 
 
 
• For example:
 
 
• Please sing louder. **(incorrect)**
 
• Please sing more loudly. **(correct)**
 
 
 
• Therefore, the correct sentence is: **Ca****n you not knock so loudly in the morning?**

**​ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Knock** means **'strike a surface noisily to attract attention.'****​**
 
• Loud is the way of sound here.

​ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e085a7f17645c801966c030eb44d69fae944b96fdb4c4077f5fba1bc2c24bc71.png] **Mistake Points__**

 
• **'Knock'** can be a **noun or verb** depending on its** usage** **in the sentence **according to which form of the other words in the sentence changes.

65:T
